stage: One-use committed migration claims and actual transactional SQL primitive
coverage: Only original newly committed claim objects carry one-use dispatch provenance; copied, modified, consumed and recovered claims cannot execute.
Actual dedicated PostgreSQL role creates and writes its owned schema, verifies in-transaction rows and acknowledges COMMIT.
Wrong bytes and nontransactional steps do not execute; Core DDL privilege errors, result denial and late BYPASSRLS elevation roll back uncommitted DDL.
Embedded COMMIT yields Unknown; it cannot be falsely declared rolled back or automatically retried.
A TCP proxy drops real PostgreSQL COMMIT CommandComplete: committed data persists, result is Unknown, and empty observation history does not permit replay.
Deadlines destroy the exclusive connection and prevent delayed preparation from dispatching.
Disconnect regression led to removing ROLLBACK on dead reserved connections; late executor queries are guarded after lifetime end.
limitations: This is an internal execution primitive; current prepare and beforeCommit admissions in execution tests are explicit fixtures.
Full governed signed installed admission, durable result Artifact/observations, cross-step recovery, nontransactional Runner, business table readiness and Enable remain incomplete.
Host must supply a fresh exclusive direct-role connection, honor callback cancellation and actually destroy the connection; failed disposal is explicitly reported.
COMMIT acknowledgement alone never constitutes migration verification or Enable.
Focused 21-test run preceded the final lifetime/query guards; the subsequent full 417-test run includes the final source.
